nutshell: The Bay Area's folk scene is old, East Bay-centred and unusually plural. Berkeley is the hub: the Freight (1968, now a $5M nonprofit hall and school), the Starry Plough's Sunday Irish sessions (up to 25 players), Ashkenaz, a weekly Monday Sacred Harp singing, and BACDS contra and English dances. San Francisco adds Changs (1938, among the oldest folk dance clubs in the US), the country's oldest public chantey sing (1981), the Plough and Stars Irish pub (1975), Hardly Strictly Bluegrass's free weekend in Golden Gate Park, and a pioneering LGBTQ+ square dance lineage. Under that sit heritage traditions few metros match: Cantonese opera since 1852, the North American birthplace of taiko, bon odori at six temples, kulintang, zydeco brought by WWII shipyard migrants, son jarocho seeded by Los Cenzontles, West African dance, Balinese gamelan. Weak spots: contra shrank after COVID, old-time jams are few, and losing space is the constant threat.

top_surprises: International folk dancing in America was effectively started in SF in Feb 1938 by Song Chang, a Chinese-American artist taught Swedish dances in a Pacific Avenue basement; the movement grew to as many as 400 California clubs and Changs still dances every Friday (http://changsfolkdancers.blogspot.com/2008/01/history-of-folk-dance-movement-in.html).

Berkeley's first Old Time Fiddlers' Convention (1968, Provo Park) was billed as the '35th Annual', with 3 lb of rutabagas for first prize and 5 lb for second; San Diego's 1970s Balboa Park contests also awarded rutabagas (https://www.berkeleyoldtimemusic.org/berkeley-farms-folkways-lp).

thesession.org lists only 9 Irish sessions inside the five counties; local volunteer calendars show 19 Irish session series (~43/month). Counting from thesession alone misses more than half the scene (https://sites.google.com/site/davbrown2/celtic).

Cooley's Reel, tune #1 on thesession.org, is named for Joe Cooley, who spent his last American years teaching long-haired Berkeley players; his partner Kevin Keegan died in SF exactly five years to the day after Cooley (https://sfcooleykeegancce.org/misc/cooley-keegan_story.html).

San Francisco is a cradle of LGBTQ+ square dancing: Foggy City Squares was dancing by 1981 and the International Association of Gay Square Dance Clubs was started in SF in 1983 (https://foggycity.org/about-foggy-city-dancers/).
Berkeley Folk Dancers dances seven nights a week and has been free for anyone under 30 since 2013 (https://berkeleyfolkdancers.org/more-facts-about-us/).

Sidney Robertson found the Potrero Hill Molokan congregation in 1938 by hearing children singing 'She'll be driving six white horses' in a church basement; she called it the most extraordinary recording of the WPA project (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/29d82f51db8848d5b62790c0854ee102).

Arhoolie Records bought its El Cerrito building with Woodstock royalties from 'I-Feel-Like-I'm-Fixin'-to-Die Rag', whose publishing Country Joe gave Chris Strachwitz as a courtesy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arhoolie_Records).

Eleven of the 20 mentors in ACTA's 2025 statewide apprenticeship cohort live in the five counties: Cantonese opera (a grandfather teaching his grandson), Taoist ritual, Shona mbira, Guinean balafon and more (https://actaonline.org/2025apprenticeships/).

The Freight, the flagship folk hall, ran a ~$940K deficit in FY2023 on 270 shows a year; its answers include a Deford Bailey festival and a 'Hip-Hop is Folk Music' initiative (https://www.berkeleyside.org/2024/03/25/berkeleys-freight-salvage-attempts-rebound-1-million-dollar-deficit).

timeline.event: John A. Stone ('Old Put') arrives overland for the Gold Rush; between 1853 and 1858 he writes 50+ songs about miners' lives and becomes 'San Francisco's foremost minstrel composer and the singing voice of the California Gold Rush'.
Hong Fook Tong gives the first Chinese (Cantonese) opera performance in the US, American Theater, Sansome St, Oct 18.

Oct 18: the Hong Fook Tong company (42 actors, financed by Canton merchants) gives the first Cantonese/Chinese opera performance in the United States at the American Theatre on Sansome Street; it plays continuously Dec 1852-Mar 1853, at one point with 123 actors.
Stone publishes 'Put's Original California Songster' in San Francisco (D.E. Appleton & Co.); it sells 'phenomenally well' and is reprinted several times.
'Put's Golden Songster' (San Francisco) prints Stone's 'Sweet Betsy from Pike', the Gold Rush ballad that entered the national folk repertoire.
Caledonian Club of San Francisco holds its first Scottish games (160th in 2026).
Caledonian Club of SF founded; first Scottish Games on Thanksgiving at Hayes Park.
Half Moon Bay Holy Ghost festa (IDES) begins.

Mandarin Theater (later Sun Sing) opens in Chinatown for Chinese opera; the rival Great China (now Great Star) Theater follows in 1925 at 636 Jackson St. The Great Star is described as the last Chinese theater in any US Chinatown.
Great Star Theater opens in Chinatown.

Georgia-born songster Jesse Fuller settles in Oakland, working for the Southern Pacific as a fireman and gandy dancer (and later as a WWII shipyard welder) before becoming the one-man band 'Lone Cat'.
Approximate first Buddhist Church of SF Bon Odori (94th held 2025).
Slim Jenkins Supper Club opens on West Oakland's 7th Street.

Feb: Song Chang teaches three couples at Bryl Wyneck's Montgomery Block studio; Changs Folk Dancers move to the Green Lantern bar (740 Kearny), then 415 Broadway. Eventually 'as many as 400 folk dance clubs' in California.
Sidney Robertson Cowell records Russian Molokan hymn singing on Potrero Hill (Sept 14).

Song Chang, a Chinese-American artist, starts an open-to-all international folk dance group in San Francisco out of Valborg 'Mama' Gravander's Scandinavian dance circle: the origin of Changs International Folk Dancers, often called the oldest continuously operating folk dance club in the US.

Sidney Robertson (later Cowell), a San Francisco native, launches the WPA Northern California Folk Music Project (1938-40), co-sponsored by the Library of Congress and UC Berkeley's Music Department, with a staff of about 20 and an office in Berkeley.

Dec 1938-Apr 1939: Azorean-born Oakland singer Alice Lemos Avila (host of a Portuguese radio hour on Oakland's KRE) records nearly 40 songs for Robertson and transcribes material for the project; Portuguese communities in Oakland and Richmond are among the collection's most represented.
Sidney Robertson Cowell launches the WPA/Library of Congress/UC Berkeley Northern California Folk Music Project (to 1940).

Robertson records the Molokan congregation of Potrero Hill, SF (Russian dissenters who came from Soviet Armenia, 'a town at the foot of Mount Ararat'); she called these recordings the 'most extraordinary' of the whole project. She also records Icelandic singers and English-language Barbary Coast songs (e.g. Byron Coffin Sr., with Mrs. Coffin on piano, in Alameda on Apr 6, 1939), Croatian gusle player and bagpipe maker Peter Boro in San Mateo, and Hungarian and Puerto Rican singers in Oakland.

Changs dancers perform at the First International Folk Dance Exhibition at the Golden Gate International Exposition on Treasure Island (1939-40), seeding California's international folk dance movement.
The California Folk Music Project ends: about 35-40 hours of recordings in 12 languages from 185 musicians, plus 168 photographs, now the Library of Congress 'California Gold' collection.
Berkeley Folk Dancers founded.
Folk Dance Federation of California formed under Buzz Glass (RSCDS-SF history says 1943); Let's Dance! magazine from 1944.
Robertson publishes 'The Recording of Folk Music in California' (UC Press). Changs formally becomes 'Changs International Folk Dancers' and moves to 1630 Stockton St., North Beach.
Maxine Blackburn organizes the Gospel Singers' Fellowship Circle at St. Paul's AME, Berkeley, linking Bay Area church choirs.
Nov 23: Reel & Strathspey Club founded in Oakland by Margaret Lamont with dancers from Changs.
Stockton Folk Dance Camp begins at College of the Pacific (79th summer in 2026).

High-schooler Dave Rothkop founds the San Francisco Folk Music Club in a tiny North Beach apartment ('the legitimate child of Hiroshima and the Cold War'); it fizzles and is restarted in 1949 via an ad in SF State's student paper.
High-schooler Dave Rothkop starts the San Francisco Folk Music Club in North Beach (relaunched 1949 at SF State).
John Filcich opens his first Balkan/folk-dance record shop.
Apr 15: KPFA Berkeley signs on, the first station of the listener-supported Pacifica network; it becomes the Bay Area's main folk/roots radio outlet.
The hungry i opens (1949 or 1950) as an 83-seat cellar at Kearny and Columbus; under Enrico Banducci (from 1951) it presents folk singers such as Stan Wilson before pivoting to comedy in 1953.
hungry i opens (1949 or 1950) in North Beach; folk singers such as Stan Wilson before comedy took over from 1953.
First Kolo Festival, a benefit for Vyts Beliajus.
Approximate start of the Kolo Festival (75th year in 2026).
The Purple Onion opens at 140 Columbus Ave, North Beach: an 80-seat cellar club that launches Phyllis Diller (1955), the Kingston Trio, the Smothers Brothers and the Irish Rovers.
Purple Onion opens in North Beach; later a stage for the Kingston Trio and Smothers Brothers.
Jesse Fuller first records 'San Francisco Bay Blues' (released by World Song in 1955); it is later covered 88+ times, from the Weavers and Peter Paul & Mary to Eric Clapton.
Accordionist Joe Cooley leaves Ireland for the US; after New York and Chicago he settles in San Francisco.
Intertribal Friendship House founded in Oakland during BIA relocation.

21-year-old Barry Olivier starts 'The Midnight Special' live folk show on KPFA and opens The Barrel, likely Berkeley's first folk-oriented instrument shop; UC told him to stop printing concert posters on red paper because of the color's communist associations.
KPFA launches the 'Midnight Special' folk show.

Late June: comedian Phyllis Diller (an Alameda housewife who had debuted at the club) cancels a week at the Purple Onion; the untested Kingston Trio fill in, and the one-week booking stretches to six months.

Berkeley's first folk clubs open on San Pablo Ave: the Steppenwolf (bought by Max Scherr, later of the Berkeley Barb) and the Blind Lemon (Rolf Cahn, a German-Jewish refugee, and Barbara Dane; Odetta on opening night).

June: the first Berkeley Folk Music Festival ('A Weekend of Folk Music') on the UC campus, directed by Barry Olivier, with Sam Hinton as MC, Jean Ritchie, Frank Warner and Billy Faier. It runs annually to 1970 and predates Newport's folk festival by a year. Same year the Kingston Trio's 'Tom Dooley' goes to No. 1.
Berkeley's first folk clubs, the Steppenwolf and the Blind Lemon (Odetta on opening night), open on San Pablo Ave; first Berkeley Folk Music Festival.

Berkeley High folkies Mayne Smith, Neil Rosenberg, Scott Hambly and Pete Berg form the Redwood Canyon Ramblers (named for a cabin in Redwood Canyon east of Oakland), the Bay Area's first bluegrass band (active to 1963). Herb Jager reorganizes the SF Folk Music Club.
Chris Strachwitz founds Arhoolie Records (first LP: Mance Lipscomb, 'Texas Sharecropper and Songster'), later based on San Pablo Ave in El Cerrito; he adds the Old Timey reissue label in 1962.

Dec 2: the Redwood Canyon Ramblers share a bill with Vern & Ray and the Carroll County Boys at Washington School, Berkeley; Vern Williams and Ray Park's Starday EP brings Arkansas/Ozark bluegrass to California.

Faith Petric takes over the SF Folk Music Club and hosts its jams at her Haight-Ashbury home for five decades. The Berkeley festival peaks at about 20,000 attendees and 35 concerts, workshops and campfires (plus a one-off Winter Festival); Bessie Jones, Roscoe Holcomb and Jean Redpath appear.

Jerry Garcia's early bluegrass/old-time bands (Hart Valley Drifters, Thunder Mountain Tub Thumpers; then the Wildwood Boys and the Black Mountain Boys with Eric Thompson in 1963) play the Peninsula and Berkeley circuit.
Faith Petric takes over the SFFMC; Malvina Reynolds writes 'Little Boxes' about Daly City.
Esther's Orbit Room opens on 7th Street.

Jan 4: the Cabale opens at 2504 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley (Rolf Cahn, Debbie Green, Howard Ziehm, Chandler Laughlin), a key stop on the Cambridge-Berkeley folk circuit; Jorma Kaukonen records there in 1964.
Cabale opens at 2504 San Pablo (Jerry Garcia plays bluegrass there); closed by 1965 as the scene moves to the Jabberwock on Telegraph.
Faith Petric starts the SFFMC newsletter 'folknik' (still published). Doc Watson, Mississippi John Hurt and Sam Hinton play a Folk Song Jamboree at Stern Grove, SF.
Faith Petric starts the folknik.
Reel & Strathspey Club becomes the RSCDS San Francisco Branch; Kopachka Folk Dancers founded in Marin.

The Cabale (renamed Cabale Creamery in Aug 1964) closes mid-1965, and the folk action moves to the Jabberwock on Telegraph Ave (bought by Bill 'Jolly Blue' Ehlert on Mar 23, 1965). On Sept 24 Country Joe and the Fish record the 'Rag Baby' EP, including 'I-Feel-Like-I'm-Fixin'-to-Die Rag', at Strachwitz's home studio. Strachwitz begins a Sunday KPFA show that runs until 1995.

With the Fillmore and Avalon paying real money, 'San Francisco folk music disappeared in a puff of green smoke' as folkies (Garcia, Kaukonen, Country Joe) went electric; the Jefferson Airplane promote the 1966 Berkeley Folk Festival.
Ali Akbar College of Music founded in Berkeley (moves to San Rafael 1968); Prince Charles Pipe Band founded.
Edwin Hawkins Singers record 'Oh Happy Day' at Ephesian Church of God in Christ, Berkeley.
First Northern California Cherry Blossom Festival; Seiichi Tanaka plays it and opens SF Taiko Dojo.
Seiichi Tanaka forms San Francisco Taiko Dojo, the first taiko ensemble in North America (NEA Heritage Fellow 2001).

Freight & Salvage opens (Nancy Owens) in a former used-furniture store at 1827 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley; first shows July 24/25. The Jabberwock closes. The first Berkeley 'old time fiddlers' convention' in Provo Park is billed as the '35th Annual', with rutabagas as prizes.
First Berkeley Old Time Fiddlers' Convention stringband contest in Provo Park, billed as the '35th Annual' (the next year was the '17th', then the '22nd').
Freight & Salvage opens on San Pablo Ave as the Jabberwock closes; first Berkeley Old Time Fiddlers' Convention, billed 'the 35th Annual', in Provo Park.

Paul Lampert opens Paul's Saloon in SF's Marina district: bluegrass seven nights a week (Mike Seeger, the New Lost City Ramblers, Vern & Ray in its first year). Barry Olivier cancels the Wild West Festival in Golden Gate Park after protests.

The last Berkeley Folk Music Festival. Mike Seeger records Berkeley's old-time bands (the New Tranquility String Band with Sue Draheim, Mac Benford and Will Spires; the Frontier with Mayne Smith) for the Folkways LP 'Berkeley Farms: Oldtime and Country Style Music of Berkeley'. Bill Monroe plays the Freight (Jan 7-8).

Kevin Keegan (Aughrim Slopes Céilí Band) moves to SF from Chicago; with Joe Cooley he teaches a generation of long-haired American players through Tuesday nights at Cooley's house, sessions at the Colby Street house in North Oakland and Saturday nights at SF's Harrington Bar (the Gráinneog Céilidh Band). The SF Comhaltas branch, later named Cooley-Keegan, starts in the early 1970s.
Kevin Keegan moves from Chicago to San Francisco.
Last Berkeley Folk Music Festival.
Mandala Folk Dance Center opens in SF (Balkan/international Thursdays).
CCÉ San Francisco branch (later Cooley-Keegan) started 'in the early 1970s' (exact year not given).
David Nadel opens Ashkenaz in a West Berkeley warehouse.
Ashkenaz opens in Berkeley.

The Starry Plough Irish pub opens in Berkeley (founded by eight volunteers including Frances Hughes); David Nadel founds Ashkenaz on San Pablo Ave; Northwestern University buys the Berkeley Folk Music Festival archive from Olivier; Old & In the Way forms. Joe Cooley dies in Ireland on Dec 20.
The Starry Plough (Berkeley) and Ashkenaz open; Joe Cooley dies in Ireland on Dec 20.
Northwestern buys the Berkeley Folk Music Festival archive; Ashkenaz and the Starry Plough open in Berkeley.

Golden State Country Bluegrass Festival (Apr 26-28) at the Marin Veterans Memorial grounds, San Rafael, with Ralph Stanley, Jimmy Martin and Old & In the Way. Ray Edlund starts 'Pig in a Pen' on KPFA (still running; hosted by Allegra Thompson since 2024).
Mickie Zekley founds Lark in the Morning as a mail-order business in San Francisco.
Lark in the Morning (mail order) and Bread & Roses (Mimi Farina) are founded.
Nick Harris starts the Stanford (Palo Alto) contra, the Bay Area's first regular contra; grows from 20-30 to 150-200 dancers in four years.
La Pena Cultural Center founded; IITC sunrise gatherings on Alcatraz begin.

Good Ol' Persons, one of the first all-women bluegrass bands (Kathy Kallick, Laurie Lewis and others), debut at a Freight open mic; La Peña Cultural Center opens next to the Starry Plough; Diamano Coura West African Dance Company is founded (Oakland).

Apr 30: the Plough and Stars opens at 116 Clement St in SF's Richmond District (per its SF Legacy Business registry file); Kevin Keegan later plays there nightly, and it becomes the city's anchor Irish session pub.
The Plough and Stars opens on Clement St (April 30, per a city Legacy Business report; medium confidence).

Strachwitz opens Down Home Music (El Cerrito); the all-women Any Old Time String Band forms; Tom Diamant's 'Panhandle Country' starts on KPFA; the Red Vest Pizza Parlor in El Cerrito becomes a bluegrass venue for a decade.
Down Home Music opens in El Cerrito.
Berkeley Morris founded by Brad Foster and others.

SFFMC presents the first San Francisco Free Folk Festival (Hall of Flowers, Golden Gate Park) and starts the Plowshares Coffeehouse series at Fort Mason (to 1998). The David Grisman Quintet (with SF-born fiddler Darol Anger) records live at the Great American Music Hall.
First SF Free Folk Festival (Hall of Flowers) and SFFMC's Plowshares Coffeehouse at Fort Mason (to 1998); Hotel Utah open mic begins.
World Arts West (SF Ethnic Dance Festival) and Kumu Hula Association of Northern California founded.
Dec 20: Kevin Keegan dies in San Francisco, five years to the day after Cooley.
Kevin Keegan dies in San Francisco on Dec 20, five years to the day after Cooley.
Carnaval SF, Gamelan Sekar Jaya and Kitka all founded.
Kitka women's vocal ensemble forms (Oakland) as an offshoot of Westwind International Folk Ensemble; Laurie Lewis founds the Grant Street String Band.
San Francisco Pipers' Club founded for uilleann pipers.
Kitka founded in Oakland; Slavyanka Men's Chorus founded in SF.
Kirston Koths starts the East Bay contra at First Congregational Church, Berkeley: $2.50 admission, 50 dancers, music by Kevin Carr and Daniel Steinberg. Starry Plough Monday céilí begins.

BACDS founded (incorporated 1982); first Playford Ball and first American Week (Mendocino Woodlands); Plowshares/SF Folk Music Center dance series at Fort Mason; Foggy City Squares performing; Barbary Coast Cloggers formed.
Ranger Dave Nettell starts the monthly chantey sing at the maritime park.
Oct 2: SF contra opens at California Hall (67 dancers), needing a police 'Dance Hall Keeper's Permit'; Western Star Dancers founded.
Oakland bluesman Brownie McGhee is in the first class of NEA National Heritage Fellows (John Lee Hooker of San Carlos follows in 1983).
East European Folklife Center founded.
Berkeley Wednesday contra begins at John Muir School; Foggy City Dancers founded; early gay square dance clubs meet in SF to form what became IAGSDC.
The Freight becomes a nonprofit (Berkeley Society for the Preservation of Traditional Music), a transition led by Mayne Smith after founder Nancy Owens stepped back.
Freight incorporates as the Berkeley Society for the Preservation of Traditional Music.
SF contra moves to St. Paul's Presbyterian (Nov).
Alasdair Fraser founds the Valley of the Moon Scottish Fiddling School (Camp Campbell, Santa Cruz Mountains, outside the MSA); kulintang master Danongan Kalanduyan moves to San Francisco.
Kulintang Arts (Kularts) founded; Danongan Kalanduyan resident director.
SF contra adds 4th Fridays, absorbing failed Point Reyes and Mill Valley series; Deer Creek Morris founded.
Alasdair Fraser places a newspaper ad that founds the San Francisco Scottish Fiddlers (now 300+ members). Apr 4: Good Ol' Persons' last show at the Red Vest.
Alasdair Fraser's newspaper ad starts the San Francisco Scottish Fiddlers.
Oakland Interfaith Gospel Choir founded.
First No Snow Ball holiday contra (grew to 200+).
The Freight moves from San Pablo Ave to a larger room on Addison St.
Freight moves to a 220-seat room on Addison St.
Mono Blanco's first Northern California visit; start of Los Cenzontles' fandango work; Eritrean festival begins in Oakland.
First All-California Sacred Harp Convention (implied by the 1995 'seventh annual'); park sea music concert series begins.
Bay Area Accordion Club (now SF Accordion Club) founded by five enthusiasts.
Paul's Saloon closes, 'an event that many consider the death of bluegrass in San Francisco'.
Marigold Project founded; Fandango Project residencies 1992-95.
Ashkenaz is designated a Berkeley Landmark (Sept 8, 1992 per the landmark list; 1993 in another source).
North Bay Country Dance Society formed.
First Pistahan; Los Cenzontles incorporates (first faculty includes Gilberto Gutierrez and banda brass teachers).

Peter Thompson's 'Bluegrass Signal' debuts on KALW (Oct 7); 'Bay Area Bluegrass' had been dropped by KCSM in 1993/94 when it went all-jazz. Kalanduyan (South SF) becomes an NEA Heritage Fellow; Ali Akbar Khan and Charles Brown (1997), Zakir Hussain (1999), Strachwitz (2000) and Tanaka (2001) follow.
Ashkenaz founder David Nadel murdered; community forms a nonprofit and buys the building.
Dec 19: Ashkenaz founder David Nadel is shot dead by an ejected patron; patrons form a nonprofit, buy the building and reopen on June 21, 1997.
Jing Ying Cantonese Opera Institute founded; ACTA founded.
Goat Hill Morris founded in SF.
The Plowshares Coffeehouse series ends; San Francisco hosts Comhaltas's 26th North American Convention.
CCÉ's 26th North American Convention held in San Francisco.
The Santa Cruz Bluegrass Society renames itself the Northern California Bluegrass Society; the Atlas Cafe (Potrero/Mission) starts weekly bluegrass on Thursdays.
First San Francisco Bluegrass (and Old-Time) Festival (Feb); Radio Valencia, home of the Sunday bluegrass night, closes in June.
Warren Hellman's free 'Strictly Bluegrass' debuts in Golden Gate Park (Hazel Dickens, Alison Krauss, Emmylou Harris); 'Hardly' is added in 2004 after Harris's non-bluegrass set.
CCÉ monthly singing session begins; Lark in the Morning sold by its founders.
Basque bertsolaris (improvising verse singers) Jesus Arriada (Daly City) and Johnny Curutchet (South SF) are named NEA National Heritage Fellows.
Suzy Thompson relaunches the Berkeley Old Time Music Convention (2004 in some accounts).
Suzy Thompson relaunches the Berkeley Old Time Music Convention in Civic Center (ex-Provo) Park with a $300 Ecology Center budget and a string band contest.

Aug 27: the Freight opens its purpose-built 490-seat hall at 2020 Addison St. SFFMC starts the El Cerrito Free Folk Festival. Folklorist Archie Green dies in SF (Mar 22). Queen Ida (Daly City) and Chitresh Das (San Rafael) are named NEA Heritage Fellows.
Freight opens its $12M Addison St building (Aug 27); first El Cerrito Free Folk Festival.
All Lark in the Morning stores (SF, Seattle, Mendocino) closed; business online only.
Esther's Orbit Room closes.
Warren Hellman dies; his heirs keep Hardly Strictly free and unsponsored (an estimated 750,000 attend that year). The 2011 SF Bluegrass & Old-Time Festival (Feb 11-20) is the last edition found.
Faith Petric dies at 98 (Oct 24); SFFMC's musical meetings move to St. Cyprian's. Fiddler Sue Draheim dies (Apr 11).
Faith Petric dies at 98; SFFMC meetings move to St. Cyprian's.
Petric's 'Fort Knox of folk music' journal collection goes to Northwestern. The documentary 'This Ain't No Mouse Music' about Arhoolie is released.
Mad Molly (Bay Area's first molly team, 1995) disbands; FFL Morris goes on hiatus.
May: the Smithsonian acquires Arhoolie Records for Smithsonian Folkways. The SF Free Folk Festival moves to Everett Middle School.
The Back Room opens in Berkeley; San Mateo folk singalong meetup begins.
Lark in the Morning bought by Eric Azumi and reopened as a Berkeley storefront (November).
Lark in the Morning reopens as a Berkeley storefront.
Oct: 'Special Techno' contra with black lights at the SF Saturday contra; Dec: 33rd No Snow Ball.
SF Chronicle feature on the Plough and Stars seisiúns (June 25).
COVID-19 halts in-person dancing; BACDS moves online (Odd Sundays English, still running); Mandala Folk Dance Center closes; North Oakland Square Dance and SF Saturday contra end.
Highland Games cancelled for the first time since 1866 (COVID).

COVID: SFFMC moves online; the Freight livestreams and plans for about 160 seats (a third of capacity); Hardly Strictly goes virtual and helps distribute $1M in musician relief. Oakland's Zakarya and Naomi Diouf (Diamano Coura) are named NEA Heritage Fellows.
COVID: SFFMC moves online (in person again from fall 2021); chantey sing goes virtual; HSB streams.
Nov 28: Hayward contra returns as an independent, vaccination-and-preregistration dance.
The fully digitized Berkeley Folk Music Festival archive (about 33,500 items, NEH-funded) goes online with Michael J. Kramer's exhibit; SFFMC resumes in-person meetings in the fall.
Richmond's Tsering Wangmo Satho (Tibetan opera, Chaksam-pa) is named an NEA Heritage Fellow; Starry Plough co-founder Frances Hughes dies.
Post-COVID: Plough session playing in the outdoor parklet from 1pm; regular Sunday evening session not yet re-established.
Chris Strachwitz dies May 5 (San Rafael); Barry Olivier dies Sept 23. The Freight runs a deficit of about $940K in FY2023 (revenue $4.9M, costs $5.9M). The BOTMC holds its 20th edition.
Chris Strachwitz dies; Down Home Music becomes a nonprofit foundation.

Aug: BACDS restarts a San Francisco contra (2nd/4th Wednesdays, Polish Club) and launches East Bay Square Dance (Aug 16, Marxist library; Hillside Club from Oct). May: Berkeley Morris's bear hobby 'Lucy' stolen with a car in Oakland.
Kularts and APICC buy 262 7th St in SoMa Pilipinas ($5M city + $3M state); Zakir Hussain dies in SF.

Catherine Hiebert Kerst's book 'California Gold' and an AFC Story Map revisit Robertson's 1930s fieldwork (April). The Starry Plough celebrates 50 years (after a GoFundMe that raised about $67K kept it alive through COVID). Barbara Dane dies in Oakland aged 97 (Oct 20); Zakir Hussain dies in December.
UICC launches 'Seisiún Saturday' in its Emerald Pub; Rose Tree Youth Céilí Band (ages 6-14) debuts at a CCÉ céilí.
Barbara Dane dies in Oakland; the Freight draws 50,000+ and launches the Deford Bailey Legacy Festival; Bread & Roses turns 50.
IAGSDC convention in SF; Kopachka turns 60; Łowiczanie turns 50; Berkeley contra returns to Wednesdays.
ACTA's 25th apprenticeship cohort (11 of 20 mentors in the five counties); 50th Alcatraz Unthanksgiving; Jing Ying's first English talkback show.
Alasdair Fraser hands the SF Scottish Fiddlers' musical direction to Caroline McCaskey (April). Bluegrass pioneer Mayne Smith dies Nov 12 in the Richmond hills.
Alasdair Fraser hands SFSF music direction to Caroline McCaskey (April); KlezCalYidFest begins; The RIC session listed.
May 11: 'Kolo John' Filcich dies at 101; May: Palo Alto Regency series ends after decades; Stockton camp moves to UC Santa Cruz; Oct: first Fog Town Hoedown; Nov: 75th Kolo Festival.
160th Highland Games; 75th Kolo Festival; bertsolari evening honoring Xalbador at the Basque Cultural Center (Oct 24).
Hardly Strictly Bluegrass runs Oct 2-4 in Hellman Hollow, still free in its 26th year.

New sessions at Mad Dog in the Fog (Feb) and O'Reilly's (Aug); SF Free Folk Festival's 50th; West Marin Fiddle Camp's final year; the Liberties bar (bluegrass jams) closes; Mayflower session moves to Sundays.
50th SF Free Folk Festival (July 11); SFFMC's in-person meetings move to a member's Panhandle flat; the Back Room turns 10.

costs.notes: BACDS contra/English/squares $25 supporter, $20 non-member, $15 member, $6 student/low-income (https://bacds.org/series/contra/berkeley_wed/); NBCDS San Rafael $15-20, first-timers free. The first East Bay contra in 1980 cost $2.50. International folk dance $5-10 (Changs $6-8, East Bay Folk Dancers $5); RSCDS classes $4-10; CCE ceili $15-20; Cajun/zydeco $20-25. Sessions, jams, Sacred Harp, the chantey sing, SFFMC meetings and both SFFMC festivals and Hardly Strictly are free; CSOTFA District 9 jam $7, East Bay Bluegrassers $5. House concerts ~$15-30 (Calliope); the house-concert figure is an estimate, not systematically checked.

surprises: International folk dancing in America was effectively started in SF in Feb 1938 by Song Chang, a Chinese-American artist taught Swedish dances in a Pacific Avenue basement; the movement grew to as many as 400 California clubs and Changs still dances every Friday (http://changsfolkdancers.blogspot.com/2008/01/history-of-folk-dance-movement-in.html).

Berkeley's first Old Time Fiddlers' Convention (1968, Provo Park) was billed as the '35th Annual', with 3 lb of rutabagas for first prize and 5 lb for second; San Diego's 1970s Balboa Park contests also awarded rutabagas (https://www.berkeleyoldtimemusic.org/berkeley-farms-folkways-lp).

thesession.org lists only 9 Irish sessions inside the five counties; local volunteer calendars show 19 Irish session series (~43/month). Counting from thesession alone misses more than half the scene (https://sites.google.com/site/davbrown2/celtic).

Cooley's Reel, tune #1 on thesession.org, is named for Joe Cooley, who spent his last American years teaching long-haired Berkeley players; his partner Kevin Keegan died in SF exactly five years to the day after Cooley (https://sfcooleykeegancce.org/misc/cooley-keegan_story.html).

San Francisco is a cradle of LGBTQ+ square dancing: Foggy City Squares was dancing by 1981 and the International Association of Gay Square Dance Clubs was started in SF in 1983 (https://foggycity.org/about-foggy-city-dancers/).
Berkeley Folk Dancers dances seven nights a week and has been free for anyone under 30 since 2013 (https://berkeleyfolkdancers.org/more-facts-about-us/).

Sidney Robertson found the Potrero Hill Molokan congregation in 1938 by hearing children singing 'She'll be driving six white horses' in a church basement; she called it the most extraordinary recording of the WPA project (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/29d82f51db8848d5b62790c0854ee102).

Arhoolie Records bought its El Cerrito building with Woodstock royalties from 'I-Feel-Like-I'm-Fixin'-to-Die Rag', whose publishing Country Joe gave Chris Strachwitz as a courtesy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arhoolie_Records).

Eleven of the 20 mentors in ACTA's 2025 statewide apprenticeship cohort live in the five counties: Cantonese opera (a grandfather teaching his grandson), Taoist ritual, Shona mbira, Guinean balafon and more (https://actaonline.org/2025apprenticeships/).

The Freight, the flagship folk hall, ran a ~$940K deficit in FY2023 on 270 shows a year; its answers include a Deford Bailey festival and a 'Hip-Hop is Folk Music' initiative (https://www.berkeleyside.org/2024/03/25/berkeleys-freight-salvage-attempts-rebound-1-million-dollar-deficit).

The Bay Area's folk-dance boom was started by a Chinese American, Song Chang, who taught three couples the schottische and Norwegian Mountain March in a Montgomery Block studio in Feb 1938; within a few years California had 'as many as 400 folk dance clubs' (http://changsfolkdancers.blogspot.com/2008/01/history-of-folk-dance-movement-in.html).

Changs' first move was to the Green Lantern bar on Kearny St, and they were thrown out the same year, reportedly because the folk dancers 'didn't spend for drinks' (http://changsfolkdancers.blogspot.com/2008/01/history-of-folk-dance-movement-in.html).

Bay Area Scottish country dancing began as a spin-off of international exhibition dancers: the founders of the 1946 Reel & Strathspey Club came from Changs, and its earliest photo shows them in Czechoslovak costumes (https://www.rscds-sf.org/about).
Berkeley Folk Dancers calls itself 'America's largest folk dance club', dances seven times a week, 50 weeks a year, and gives free membership to anyone under 30 (https://berkeleyfolkdancers.org/).

When the SF contra opened at California Hall in 1982, the organizer had to get a police 'Dance Hall Keeper's Permit' and monthly one-day beer licenses; on drag-show nights, dozens of leather-clad bikers lined the street as security and helped carry the sound gear (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IiNj4uEUK_PKeKUdY6dM5U_QOcG3n49p/view).
Legend says early Berkeley contra dancers skinny-dipped in the UC pool during the break; BACDS has 'no official comment on those rumors' (https://bacds.org/series/contra/).

San Francisco is where the gay square dance movement organized: early clubs met in SF in 1983 to form what became the International Association of Gay Square Dance Clubs, and one 1970s exhibition group (Foggy City Squares) spawned a clogging team and two square dance clubs (https://foggycity.org/about-foggy-city-dancers/).

The new East Bay Square Dance held its first night (Aug 2024) in the Niebyl-Proctor Marxist Library, where the beloved North Oakland Square Dance had run for a decade before the pandemic (https://bacds.org/series/contra/).
Berkeley Morris's bear hobby-horse 'Lucy' was stolen along with a team member's car in Oakland on May 2 2024 and is still missing; the team offers a reward (https://berkeleymorris.org/).

Morris teams bookend the season with the sun: Berkeley Morris 'dances the sun up' at Inspiration Point at 5:20 am on May 1, Goat Hill does the same on Twin Peaks, and both dance the sun down at Sutro Heights on the solstice (https://berkeleymorris.org/performances/).
'Kolo John' Filcich, who founded the Kolo Festival in 1952, died May 11 2026 at 101, six months before the festival's 75th edition (https://sfdh.us/encyclopedia/filcich_j.html).

Ashkenaz's dance floor is maple from the old Hudson pencil factory in San Leandro, paid for plank by plank; its founder David Nadel was murdered in 1996 by a patron he had ejected (https://www.ashkenaz.com/history).
The Polish Club in the Mission hosts both the revived SF contra (Wednesdays) and the RSCDS San Francisco Scottish class (Thursdays) (https://www.rscds-sf.org/classes).
The annual Lord of the Rings Square Dance at Ashkenaz (4th edition Oct 31 2026) has Skillet Licorice playing as 'Denethor's Supper' (https://www.bacds.org/).

Every BACDS contra and the East Bay Square are now gender-neutral (Larks/Robins or 'dance any role'), and the Hayward contra still keeps COVID data-dashboard pages on its website (https://sfbaycontra.org/).
Just outside the MSA, a 'clothing optional' contra was held at Lupin Lodge in the Santa Cruz Mountains in July 2026 (https://bacds.org/calendars/2026/07/).

California's folk-arts apprenticeship money pools in the Bay: 11 of the 20 mentor-apprentice pairs ACTA funded statewide in 2025 have a mentor living in the five counties, covering Cantonese opera, Lung Moon Taoist ritual, Tahitian drumming, Guinean balafon, Shona mbira, Haitian dance, Carnatic drumming, capoeira angola and Mexican folk harp (https://actaonline.org/2025apprenticeships/).

On Oct 24, 2026, two star bertsolaris from the Basque Country improvised sung verses in South San Francisco on assigned topics including 'using driverless taxis' and over-packed suitcases, in an evening honoring Xalbador, whose granddaughters (Aire Ahizpak) sang his verses (https://sfbasqueculturalcenter.org/blog/xalbador-gogoratuz).

One fairground in Pleasanton hosts the 160-year-old Scottish Highland Games (https://thescottishgames.com/home), a hula competition billed as the oldest hula festival outside Hawai'i (https://tricityvoice.com/hula-takes-center-stage-at-pleasanton-fairgrounds/) and Navratri garba nights for thousands (https://www.gcabayarea.org/).

Cantonese opera at Jing Ying is a four-generation family affair: founder Xiu Ben Chen played with his wife, his father Ziping and his son Kelan in one 2025 piece, and in 2025 ACTA funded grandfather Ziping to teach grandson Kelan (https://www.windnewspaper.com/article/jing-ying-institute-shares-the-beauty-of-cantonese-opera-with-wider-communities-by-launching-its-first-talkback-show).

North American taiko began with a complaint: Seiichi Tanaka found SF's 1967 Cherry Blossom Festival too quiet, apprenticed in Japan, and came back to drum at the 1968 festival (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Taiko_Dojo).

Old heritage websites are being taken over: Kularts' former domain kularts.org now redirects to an unrelated Japanese site (Kularts moved to kularts-sf.org), and the Croatian American Cultural Center's own /about page now serves Thai slot-machine ads (https://croatianamericanweb.org/about/).

The Bay Area's zydeco scene still ran about 12 dances inside the five counties in Oct 2026, many at an Eagles Hall in El Cerrito; it traces to Louisiana Creoles who came for wartime shipyard jobs, like Queen Ida, still alive at 97 (https://sfczcalendar.com/, https://www.arts.gov/honors/heritage/queen-ida-guillory).

The Bay's son jarocho fandango revival has a start date: Eugene Rodriguez met Mono Blanco in 1989, and Chris Strachwitz recorded them for Arhoolie on that first trip (https://www.loscenzontles.com/fandango-project/).

Only eight competing pipe bands are registered in the whole WUSPBA Northern Branch for 2026, three of them in the MSA, despite the region hosting California's largest Highland Games (https://wuspbanb.org/bands/).

The SF Basque Club's June picnic, long a South San Francisco fixture, moved out of the MSA to Penngrove (Sonoma County) in 2025 (https://sfbasqueculturalcenter.org/events-page/basque-club-picnic-yzd52).

The Highland Games ran through the 1906 earthquake, the Depression and both World Wars; COVID in 2020 was the only interruption in 160 years (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Highland_Gathering_and_Games).

A folklorist recorded Russian Molokan hymn singing on Potrero Hill on Sept 14, 1938; her caption says the photographed group was 'less than a quarter of the total adult group' (https://www.loc.gov/item/2017701287/).

Comedian Phyllis Diller, an Alameda housewife, made the Kingston Trio: her cancelled week at the Purple Onion in June 1957 went to the untested Trio, and it stretched to six months. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kingston_Trio

The Session's tune #1, 'Cooley's', is named for an accordionist who spent his last American years in San Francisco, teaching hippies on Tuesday nights after his wife Nancy's cake and Patricia Kennelly's accordion lesson. https://joecooleytapes.org/

Berkeley's 1968 old-time fiddlers' convention was billed as the '35th Annual'. First prize was 3 lb of rutabagas, second prize 5 lb, bribes were openly solicited, and a 40-piece instant band was 'disqualified for unlawful assembly'. https://www.berkeleyoldtimemusic.org/berkeley-farms-folkways-lp

Sidney Robertson found the Potrero Hill Molokan church because on a Sunday walk she heard children in its basement singing 'She'll be driving six white horses when she comes'. She later called the congregation's recordings the 'most extraordinary' of the whole WPA project. https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/29d82f51db8848d5b62790c0854ee102

Berkeley's Folk Music Festival (1958) predates Newport by a year, and Pete Seeger and Alan Lomax, who came to Berkeley in 1959, then sat on Newport's board. https://sites.northwestern.edu/bfmf/the-early-years/

The anti-war anthem 'I-Feel-Like-I'm-Fixin'-to-Die Rag' was recorded in Chris Strachwitz's home studio in 1965, and its Woodstock royalties bankrolled Arhoolie's documentation of blues, norteño and Cajun music. https://www.chickenonaunicycle.com/Jabberwock%20History.htm

UC Berkeley told Barry Olivier to stop printing folk concert posters on red paper in the 1950s because the color suggested communism. https://sites.northwestern.edu/bfmf/barry-olivier-festival-director/

The first Chinese opera ever performed in the US was in San Francisco on Oct 18, 1852, and SF's Great Star Theater (1925) is the last Chinese theater left in any American Chinatown. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Star_Theater

Berkeley's coffeehouse folk scene was partly a product of liquor law: limits on alcohol sales within a mile of campus kept jazz nightclubs in SF and left Berkeley with 'folk music and strong coffee'. https://www.chickenonaunicycle.com/Jabberwock%20History.htm

The Berkeley Folk Music Festival's archive is in Evanston, Illinois: Northwestern bought it from Olivier in 1973, through a bookseller who sat on the Berkeley City Council during People's Park. https://sites.northwestern.edu/bfmf/foreword/

The Bay Area's NEA Heritage Fellows lean toward diaspora classical and ritual arts rather than Anglo-American folk: two Hindustani masters (Ali Akbar Khan and Zakir Hussain, both listed in San Anselmo), two Basque bertsolaris (Daly City and South SF, 2003), a kulintang master, a taiko founder and a Tibetan opera singer. https://arcgis.github.io/storymaps-heritage-fellows-data/artists.csv
A zydeco queen lived in Daly City: 'Queen' Ida Guillory, the first woman to lead a zydeco band, was an NEA Heritage Fellow listed in San Mateo County. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Ida

The Bay Area bluegrass scene was unusually female-led early: Good Ol' Persons (1975) and the Any Old Time String Band (1976) were all-women bands, and Laurie Lewis recalls 'there weren't a lot of cutting contests'. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurie_Lewis

Jerry Garcia's pre-Dead bands included the Thunder Mountain Tub Thumpers, the Hart Valley Drifters and the Asphalt Jungle Mountain Boys (with Jody Stecher and Eric Thompson). https://www.bgsignal.com/bay-area-bluegrass-history-1959-2001.html

The Starry Plough was founded in 1973 as a safe space for political refugees from Ireland, Chile and Honduras; so many Chileans came that some bought the building next door, which became La Peña Cultural Center. https://www.berkeleyside.org/2024/03/13/starry-plough-irish-pub-berkeley-50-years
The San Francisco Bluegrass & Old-Time Festival's old domain, sfbluegrass.org, now serves Indonesian online-gambling spam. http://web.archive.org/web/20200606042745/http://www.sfbluegrass.org:80/
Kevin Keegan died in San Francisco on Dec 20, 1978, five years to the day after his friend Joe Cooley. https://sfcooleykeegancce.org/misc/cooley-keegan_story.html
Mad Dog in the Fog's first-Sunday Irish session gives players free drinks up to a $100 tab (https://thesession.org/sessions/9633).

The first Berkeley Old Time Fiddlers' Convention (Provo Park, 1968) was billed as the '35th Annual'; the next year's was the '17th' and the one after the '22nd' (https://www.berkeleyoldtimemusic.org/about).

Kevin Keegan died in San Francisco on Dec 20 1978, five years to the day after Joe Cooley; Keegan had first played SF at the Carousel Ballroom before playing nightly at the Plough (https://sfcooleykeegancce.org/misc/cooley-keegan_story.html).

One Berkeley pub, the Starry Plough, hosts about 15 participatory slots a month (plus a weekly Monday céilí): two weekly Irish sessions, a twice-monthly kids session, plus monthly bluegrass, old-time 'Shred Sesh', accordion/zydeco jams and an Irish-language 'Pop-up Gaeltacht' (https://thestarryplough.com/sunday-irish-music-session/).
The Starry Plough's third-Sunday late session is a FairPlé session led by women, part of the Irish gender-balance movement (https://thestarryplough.com/sunday-irish-music-session/).

An old-time jam meets in the Irish 'Home of Traditional Irish Music' (Plough and Stars) on odd Tuesdays, and its even-Tuesday twin has lived on Zoom since the pandemic (https://sites.google.com/site/davbrown2/oldtimesf).

Bay Area bluegrass runs a parallel invitation-only 'JamBot' circuit: Tam Jam (Sausalito), Point Jam (Point Richmond), Hop Jam (Half Moon Bay) and the Taco Jam in an Oakland taqueria, about 16 invitational jams a month (https://jambot.org/JamBots/TacoJam/).
A monthly old-time jam meets on the 5th floor of the Berkeley Public Library (https://www.berkeleyoldtimemusic.org/spring-situation-2026).
The weekly East Bay Bluegrassers jam meets upstairs in a music store, Rockin' Robbie's in El Cerrito (https://californiabluegrass.org/event/wednesday-east-bay-bluegrassers-jam/all/).
Session host Alina Larson only started the uilleann pipes on May 21 2020, and now co-hosts with All-Ireland slow-air champion Blake Ritter (https://www.ceol-sa-cheo.com/).
The Half Moon Bay slow session meets in a yacht club, so visitors need a guest pass (https://thesession.org/sessions/9728).

thesession.org lists only 9 Irish sessions inside the five counties, while local calendars yield about 19 Irish session series, so it misses more than half (https://www.sffmc.org/community-folk-calendar/).

The SF Scottish Fiddlers (300+ members) meet from San Jose to Healdsburg to Nevada City and play Galician, Breton, Scandinavian and Quebecois tunes, not just Scottish ones (https://www.sfscottishfiddlers.org/About-the-SFSF).

Lark in the Morning, the world-instrument shop founded in SF in 1974, died as a chain by 2010 and was reborn in Berkeley in 2017; one employee bought her first fiddle there aged 11 and busked beside the Fisherman's Wharf store (https://larkinthemorning.com/pages/about-us).
Dublin, California (Alameda County) has a jam every Tuesday of the month in a historic schoolhouse: Irish/Celtic on odd Tuesdays, bluegrass on even ones (https://groups.io/g/dublinirishjam).

The first Berkeley Old Time Fiddlers' Convention (1968) was billed 'the 35th Annual', followed by the 22nd and then the 17th; first prize was 3 lbs of rutabagas and second prize 5 lbs. https://www.berkeleyoldtimemusic.org/berkeley-farms-folkways-lp

SFFMC's founder called the club 'the legitimate child of Hiroshima and the Cold War'; he started it as a high-school student in 1948, and it is still meeting 78 years later. https://www.sffmc.org/history/
At the 50th SF Free Folk Festival (2026) the best-attended workshop was the sea shanty workshop. https://www.sffmc.org/folknik/

The SF maritime park's chantey sing (since 1981) is billed as the nation's oldest; every sing opens with 'Away Rio' ('Sing fare-thee-well my Frisco girl'), and the house rules were 'no drinking, no smoking, no falling off the pier'. https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/chantey-sing-san-francisco

Faith Petric's hoard of folk-music journals, 'the Fort Knox of folk music', went to Northwestern University in Illinois in 2014, joining the Berkeley Folk Music Festival archive that Northwestern bought in 1973. https://sites.northwestern.edu/bfmf/foreword/

UC Berkeley told festival director Barry Olivier not to print folk concert posters on red paper, because of the color's association with communism. https://sites.northwestern.edu/bfmf/barry-olivier-festival-director/

The Freight, which began in 1968 as an 87-seat coffeehouse in a former used-furniture store, had $5.28M in revenue and 50,000+ visitors in 2024. https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/942887073

When the Freight got big, a pianist built a 100-seat room full of thrift-store couches specifically to recreate the old Freight (the Back Room, 2016). https://48hills.org/2026/04/one-decade-in-the-back-room-still-holds-space-for-intimate-musical-encounters/

Bay Area Sacred Harp singers already use the new 2025 Edition, and they hold a monthly Christian Harmony singing online over the low-latency Jamulus software. https://bayareasacredharp.org/local-singings/
'Oh Happy Day' (Edwin Hawkins Singers) was recorded in 1967 in a Berkeley church, Ephesian Church of God in Christ. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh_Happy_Day
Malvina Reynolds' 'Little Boxes' ('ticky-tacky') is about Daly City, inside this MSA. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Boxes
Chris Strachwitz of El Cerrito's Arhoolie Records received the NEA's first-ever 'keeper of tradition' National Heritage Fellowship (FY2000). https://www.arts.gov/honors/heritage/chris-strachwitz

Hardly Strictly Bluegrass is free and refuses all sponsors; its 2011 crowd (~750,000 over three days) was 'nearly equal' to San Francisco's population. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardly_Strictly_Bluegrass

The 1948 folk club's in-person musical meeting now happens in a member's flat because the club lost its church hall: 12-16 people, against ~100 at Faith Petric's house in the 1970s. https://www.sffmc.org/musical-meetings/
The Bazaar Cafe open mic bans covers (unless public domain) and amplification, and lets performers book a specific time slot a week in advance. https://www.bayareaopenmics.com/OM-BAZAARCAFE.html
The SF maritime park's virtual chantey sing has raised $29,480 from 714 supporters. https://givebutter.com/ChanteySing
curiosities: The rutabaga prize appears in Berkeley's 1968 mock fiddle convention and San Diego's 1970s Balboa Park contests. Was there a West Coast 'anti-contest' movement, who spread it (the Berkeley Farms LP? Lou Curtiss?), and did other metros have one?

SF had no regular contra from 2020 to Aug 2024 and the East Bay's founding contra is still on hiatus, while international folk dance clubs carried on. Across all 20 metros, which dance forms came back after COVID and what predicts it (hall ownership, gender-neutral calling, a younger queer-led wave)?
How badly does thesession.org undercount Irish sessions in each metro? SF's ratio is roughly 9 listed to 19 found on local calendars.

Is the Bay Area's huge count of NEA Heritage Fellows (~15 in five counties, against 1 in San Diego) a product of nominating infrastructure (ACTA, Arhoolie, UC Berkeley) or of real differences in traditions?

Old-time music in the Bay Area seems to be growing through square-dance revivals (Feral Friday, East Bay Square, the Lord of the Rings square) rather than jams. Is the square dance the main old-time growth vector elsewhere too?
Which metros have a public, permanent maritime chantey sing? SF has run one since 1981; navy-port San Diego has none.
Do folk institutions survive better as nonprofits that own their buildings (Ashkenaz, the Freight, Kularts' 2024 purchase) than as renters? Compare closure rates across metros.

SF lost its long-running Saturday-night contra in 2020 and only got a contra back in Aug 2024, on a Wednesday. Did other big-city cores lose their weekend contra while weeknight or suburban series survived?
Hayward broke away from BACDS over COVID protocols. How many other cities have a COVID-cautious splinter dance, and are they still going in 2026?
The Bay Area has about 26 modern Western square dance clubs but only one monthly old-time square dance. Is that ratio typical, and are club numbers falling as fast here as in other metros?
SF was central to LGBTQ square dancing (IAGSDC 1983). Which other metros have LGBTQ square, clogging or country-western clubs older than 40 years?
The 1940s California folk-dance boom ('as many as 400 clubs'): did other metros have a founding figure like Song Chang, and how many of those clubs are left in each city?

Berkeley Folk Dancers says it is 'America's largest folk dance club' with only 100+ members. What is the largest international folk dance club in each metro, and has the number of members gone up or down?
Pub céilí dancing every week since 1980 (Starry Plough): which other US cities have a weekly céilí in a pub, and how old are they?
Morris teams: how many active teams does each metro have per million people, and how many cities have a May Day sunrise tradition?

Contra admission rose from $2.50 (1980) to $20 (2026), roughly double the inflation-adjusted 1980 price (about $10 today, by a rough CPI estimate). How do admission prices compare across metros relative to local incomes?
Israeli folk dance has had weekly sessions in SF since the 1960s. Which metros still have weekly Israeli dancing, and are dancers getting older?
International folk dance in the Bay Area mostly uses recorded music, while contra always has live bands. Does that split hold in other cities, and does it affect how many young people come?
How many ACTA-style state apprenticeship awards go to each metro relative to population, and does the Bay's dominance reflect tradition density or proximity to ACTA's SF office?

Do other metros have a single event space like the Alameda County Fairgrounds that hosts unrelated diaspora mega-events (Highland games, hula, garba)? Which venues anchor diaspora calendars elsewhere?
Why is youth mariachi education so much thinner in the SF-Oakland MSA than in San Jose, Los Angeles or Texas? Is it district policy, demographics or the lack of a university program?
How many urban Obon festivals with public bon odori run in each metro (Seattle, LA, Sacramento, Denver, Chicago)? Is the Bay's count of six or more unusual outside Hawai'i and LA?
Which other metros have Louisiana Creole zydeco scenes created by WWII shipyard migration (Houston obviously, but also LA and Seattle-Tacoma), and are they growing or shrinking?
How many heritage organizations in each metro have lost their web domains to spam, and does that predict organizational decline or just volunteer turnover?
Is the son jarocho fandango revival (Los Cenzontles 1989, LA's Fandango sin Fronteras, Seattle) stronger where a 1990s residency seeded it?
Where else do Holy Ghost festas with chamarrita survive (San Diego's Point Loma, the Central Valley, New Bedford/Fall River), and how do they compare with Half Moon Bay's 155-year run?
Are tamburica festivals dying nationally or only in SF? Compare Pittsburgh, Chicago and Detroit.
Which metros host a Balkan/international folk dance festival as old as the Kolo Festival (75 years)?
Do cities with a strong pipe band youth program (Prince Charles, 1967) keep more pipers in the scene? How many competing pipe bands per million people in each metro?
How many metros have a living Cantonese opera institute, and is SF's the oldest continuous Chinese opera city in the US (since 1852)?
Which other metros had a Gold Rush-era printed songster tradition like Put's (e.g. Denver/Colorado mining songsters), and did any of those songs enter the session/jam repertoire?

Robertson's WPA project recorded 185 musicians in 12 languages across Northern California; how does that compare with other WPA/LoC regional surveys (e.g. Wisconsin 1937, Florida WPA) in breadth, and which metros have the richest 1930s field recordings of their own immigrant communities?

Berkeley's folk clubs (Blind Lemon, Cabale, Jabberwock) died within about 10 years, but the Freight (1968) survived; what made the 'late, nonprofit' clubs last in other cities too (Club Passim in Boston, Ark in Ann Arbor, Old Town School in Chicago)?

Paul's Saloon's 1991 closing was called 'the death of bluegrass in SF'; did other dense, high-rent cities lose their dedicated bluegrass bars at the same time, and where did those scenes move (suburbs, cafés, festivals)?

The Bay Area produced unusually many all-women string bands in the 1970s (Good Ol' Persons, Any Old Time, later the Stairwell Sisters); is the share of women bandleaders in old-time/bluegrass measurably higher in the Bay Area than in other metros?

Free, unsponsored mega-festivals: Hardly Strictly (750K in 2011) depends on one family foundation. Are there comparable philanthropically endowed free folk festivals elsewhere, and what happened to them after the founder died?

The Freight ran a ~$940K deficit in FY2023 with 270 shows a year and a 70-person staff; how do post-COVID finances compare across the big nonprofit folk listening rooms (Ark, Passim, Old Town, McCabe's, Caffè Lena)?

Several Irish tradition bearers (Cooley, Keegan) passed through Chicago before SF; did the Chicago-to-SF migration path shape the Bay Area's Irish repertoire (e.g. Galway/East Clare box styles) compared with Boston's or New York's?

How many tunes are named for each of the 20 metros on The Session and in TTA? San Francisco gets a Charlie Lennon reel and an Alasdair Fraser jig but nothing for Oakland; does city-naming track touring or tune-composer residence?

Berkeley's original fiddlers' convention mocked competition (rutabaga prizes); do other metros' revival-era contests show the same anti-contest ethos, and does that correlate with fewer fiddle contests today?

Which metros have NEA Heritage Fellows whose traditions (Hindustani classical, taiko, kulintang, Basque bertsolari) are absent from their city's 'folk' self-image, and is the Bay Area unusual in this?

Bay Area Irish sessions cluster on Sunday afternoons and early evenings (Plough 1pm, Starry 5:30 and 7:30, Sláinte, Mad Dog). Is that a post-COVID shift, and do other metros show the same move from late nights to daytime?
Invitational 'JamBot' bluegrass jams (Tam, Point, Hop, Taco) make up about a third of Bay Area bluegrass jam slots. Does this model exist in other metros?
How badly does thesession.org undercount sessions in each metro compared with local calendars? Here it misses more than half.
Which other metros have FairPlé (women-led) Irish sessions?
The Bay Area has about 30 open bluegrass jam slots a month against about 12 old-time, yet old-time has the deeper institutional history (BOTMC since 1968). Is that ratio typical?
Are there other cities with a 300-member Scottish fiddle club, and does the SFSF model (monthly meetings in homes, annual concert tour) exist elsewhere?
Several metros' session info now rests on one or two volunteer calendar keepers (David Brown, Peter Thompson, Shelby Solomon here). How fragile is this?
Old-time jams in public libraries (Berkeley): does any other metro do this?
Scandinavian music sessions seem to have faded in the East Bay since COVID while they survive on the Peninsula. Is that true, and why?
Why are pre-dance jams (Feral Friday, East Bay Square Dance) the growth area for old-time in SF/Berkeley, and is the same true of square-dance revivals elsewhere?

How many other US metros have a continuously running public chantey sing that predates the 2021 TikTok shanty boom, and did the boom raise attendance in SF (the 2026 SF Free Folk Festival's best-attended workshop was shanties)?

Folk clubs founded in the 1940s-50s (SFFMC 1948, Seattle, Portland, LA's Songmakers): which still hold in-person song circles, and what are their attendance trends since COVID? SFFMC is down to 12-16 in person and 15-20 on Zoom.

Is the Freight's arc (87-seat coffeehouse to a $5M, 450-490-seat nonprofit) typical of surviving 1960s folk rooms (Club Passim, Caffe Lena, Ark), and does a small 'replacement room' like the Back Room appear wherever the original scales up?
Which metros already use the 2025 Sacred Harp edition locally, and how many weekly (rather than monthly) singings does each big metro have?
Do other cities have a weekend public-radio folk block as large as KPFA + KALW (~11 hours), and how many hosts have been on air for 40+ years like Peter Thompson?
Where else do free, unsponsored mega-festivals exist (Hardly Strictly), and what happens to them when the founding patron dies?
How common are long-running 'originals only' and 'no-PA' open mics like Bazaar Cafe's, and are open mics dated to the 1970s (Hotel Utah, 1977) found in other metros?

Bay Area folk has a strong archive diaspora (Berkeley festival and Petric collections at Northwestern; Arhoolie at the Smithsonian). Which other metros lost their key folk archives to out-of-state institutions?
Is there still a living small-group Black gospel quartet circuit (anniversary programs) in Oakland/Richmond, as in Houston, Memphis or Birmingham?
How do house-concert densities compare between metros, and is there a platform-level count (Concerts in Your Home, TicketTailor, Meetup)?
data_quality_notes: MERGE NOTES: Merged from separate research threads (sessions/trad, dance, song, heritage, history); duplicates across threads were merged by name and conflicting values noted in notes fields. Unverified events were moved to defunct. Facebook and Instagram were not checked directly; thesession.org and Nominatim were rate-limited, so most lat/lng are null; tunearch.org and slippery-hill.com blocked automated searches. THREAD NOTES: [sf-dance.json] web_search was heavily rate-limited, so the census leans on primary calendars: the BACDS monthly calendars (May-Dec 2026), the Ashkenaz Venuepilot calendar (Jan-Dec 2026, GraphQL API), the Folk Dance Federation events API and directory listings, the NBCDS events API, the RSCDS-SF class page and the SCVSDA square dance directory (updated 24 Oct 2026). Modern Western square dance clubs are from one directory and were not checked club by club (medium confidence). Facebook-only scenes (Cajun/zydeco calendars, Bay Area bal folk) could not be checked; no recurring bal folk was found. Some FDF listings have text from 2022 (Balkan Dance Cabal, Tamil group) and may be stale. Membership counts are rarely published (BFD 'over 100'; BACDS, RSCDS and FDF give none). No Bay Area demographic survey was found; CDSS's 2023 Generational Transition Survey (829 responses aged 18-44) is national only. Founding years for Café Shalom (1960s), East Bay Folk Dancers (early 1960s), Festival of the Oaks (counted back from its 77th edition) and Eszterlánc (from an email handle) are approximate. FDF founding year: its own list gives 1942-43 for the first president's term, but the RSCDS-SF history says 1943. The Starry Plough page gives both $10 and $5 as the suggested donation. Per-month totals include team practices and club class nights, which inflate the numbers compared with public dances. The Palo Alto contra, Playford Ball, camps and South Bay series are outside the MSA (Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Sonoma counties) and are flagged. [sf-heritage.json] Web search was heavily rate-limited (shared quota), so this thread used about 35 searches and 90+ direct fetches. Several key sites block automated fetches (La Pena: 403 including its events API; Nichi Bei: 403; loc.gov HTML: 403, JSON partly) or are compromised or lapsed (kularts.org, parts of croatianamericanweb.org; bcsfweb.org, which a guess suggested belonged to the Buddhist Church of SF, now hosts lottery spam, but its ownership was not verified). Evidence for La Pena's recurring bomba and rumba events comes from search snippets and third-party listings (2025), not La Pena's own calendar. Many founding years are inferred from anniversary counts ('94th', '75th', '45th', '14th', '29th') and should be treated as plus or minus one year. Not investigated or not found in this pass: Armenian, Polish, Ukrainian and Serbian music practice; Hmong (no Hmong-specific music organization found in the five counties); Andean and Salvadoran/Nicaraguan groups; Georgian and Bulgarian choirs other than Kitka; Japanese minyo groups; Indonesian (Javanese) gamelan; Irish dance schools and Comhaltas (left to the trad thread); mariachi school programs in Oakland and Richmond (none found). Attendance figures are mostly absent; Carnaval's '100,000+' and the garba '5,000+' figures come from search summaries, not primary sources. NEA fellow locations are taken from the NEA's state-filtered list (it records place at time of award). ACTA counts are from the 2022-2025 cohort pages; 'five-county' includes a pair when either the mentor or the apprentice lives in SF, Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin or San Mateo, except the 2025 count of 11, which counts mentors only. Several heritage traditions (Afghan, Tongan/Samoan, Ethiopian) are clearly practiced at weddings and in churches and community events but are thinly documented online, so their vitality ratings are low-confidence. [sf-history.json] Thread scope: history, people, archives, defunct, tunes. Research used only web search/fetch (no browser). Several key primary sites block automated fetches (loc.gov collection pages 403; thefreight.org 403; tunearch.org 403; slippery-hill.com 410; folkways.si.edu 403), so Library of Congress detail comes via the AFC Folklife Today blog (2024) and the AFC ArcGIS Story Map JSON, and the Freight's history comes via Berkeleyside, the Grammy site, the Berkeley plaque project and bgsignal. The web_search tool was heavily rate-limited (shared across parallel threads), which limited verification of second-tier names. People named in the brief but NOT verified for this file (omitted or flagged): Kevin Carr, Erik Hoffman (seen calling 2023 BOTMC square dance per Berkeleyside), Evie Ladin (Stairwell Sisters founder per Berkeleyside snippet), Keith Terry, Paul Kotapish, Rushad Eggleston (Bay connection not verified), Jeremy Kittel and Natalie Haas (Haas grew up in Palo Alto, outside the MSA; not verified), Tom Sauber and Richard Greene (LA; Greene played in the Bay Area Pine Valley Boys in 1964), Bruce Molsky (not Bay). Lark in the Morning: Mickie Zekley's Irish interest came from Cooley and Keegan (CCÉ); Lark's locations and SF retail history were not verified. Starry Plough is ACTIVE (50th anniversary 2024), not defunct. Source disagreements: (1) Freight's original address is 1827 San Pablo Ave in the Berkeley plaque, bgsignal-linked and search sources (the brief's 'Grove Street' and 'founded by Nicholas Seeger' were not supported; the founder was Nancy Owens). (2) Freight moves: 1988 to a 'slightly larger' Addison St room, then Aug 27, 2009 to the 490-seat 2020 Addison St (Grammy says '400-plus seat'). (3) Blind Lemon founding: 1958 (plaque) vs 'mid 1950s' (chickenonaunicycle). (4) Joe Cooley's US arrival: 1953 (joecooleytapes), 1954 (Wikipedia) or 1957 (CCÉ photo caption); CCÉ says he came to SF in the early 1970s while Wikipedia implies earlier; he spent 18 years in America. (5) The 1969 and 1970 joke numbering of the Provo Park fiddlers' convention ('17th' vs '22nd') differs between the BOTMC site and Rita Weill's 1971 notes. (6) Ashkenaz landmark: Sept 8, 1992 (landmark list) vs 1993 (cited article). (7) Strictly Bluegrass 2001 date: bgsignal says Oct 27, 2001; Wikipedia gives the first weekend of October as the current slot. (8) The Colby Street house is placed in Berkeley (joecooleytapes) or North Oakland (Wikipedia, Sue Draheim); Colby St straddles the line. (9) WPA project size: '35 hours' (Wikipedia) vs '40 hours' (AFC 2024). The SF Bluegrass & Old-Time Festival end date (2011) is inferred from the frozen website (Wayback 2020 snapshot still announcing Feb 2011) and is medium confidence. NEA Heritage Fellow locations come from the NEA/Esri dataset (to 2021) and AFS/ACTA announcements (2020, 2022); no Bay Area fellow was found for 2023-2025 (search-based, medium confidence). Non-music fellows (quilters Gussie Wells and Arbie Williams, Oakland 1991; papel picado artist Herminia Albarrán Romero, SF 2005) exist; only Albarrán Romero is listed in people. Tunes: The Session API was searched for San Francisco, Berkeley, Oakland, Golden Gate, Tamalpais, Marin, Alameda, Sausalito, Presidio, Barbary and Frisco; TTA and Slippery-Hill could not be queried, so old-time titles may be missing. Barbary Coast songs: the one named singer (Byron Coffin Sr., Alameda, Apr 6, 1939, LoC item 2017700892) comes from a search summary because loc.gov blocks fetches; medium confidence. Plough and Stars opening (Apr 30, 1975) comes from a search summary of SF Legacy Business documents; the same summary says Bob Heaney founded it and was the Starry Plough's original owner, which conflicts with the Starry Plough's own account of eight volunteer co-founders. [sf-sessions.json] Counts are for the five MSA counties (SF, Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, San Mateo); notable events in Santa Clara, Sonoma, Solano and Santa Cruz counties are listed separately with outside_msa:true and excluded from totals. Main evidence came from four volunteer-maintained calendars all updated in Oct 2026: the SFFMC community folk calendar (10/20/26), David Brown's CelticSF and OldtimeSF calendars (10/26/26) and Peter Thompson's Bluegrass Signal jam list (Nov 2026 items); plus venue sites (Plough and Stars Oct 2026 calendar, Starry Plough pages), the CBA calendar (Sept-Oct 2026) and thesession.org (11 sessions within 40 miles of Oakland, 9 inside the MSA). These aggregators disagree on several details (Starry kids session 2nd/4th vs 3rd Sunday; Baygrass Starry jam 2nd Sunday vs 2nd Saturday; SFSF 3rd vs 2nd Sunday; Bernal jam 4th vs 2nd & 4th Sundays; UICC slow session last vs 4th Saturday), noted per event. Several jams rest on a single listing (Winters Tavern Pacifica, Atlas Cafe, Hali's potluck, La Peña family jam, Alhambra Irish House). Invitational jams are counted but reported separately. The 'Woodhouse Brewing' Tuesday jam was excluded because it is probably in Santa Cruz. web_search was heavily rate-limited (shared quota), so Facebook/Instagram evidence was not checked directly; the Freight's website returned 403 and tunearch.org blocked automated access (Cloudflare), so tune research relied on thesession.org's API. Nominatim also returned 429, so only thesession venues have coordinates. No 2024-26 evidence was found for East Bay Scandinavian sessions, Greek jams, open klezmer jams, harp circles or hammered-dulcimer clubs inside the MSA. Cape Breton music is covered only through the SFSF; no dedicated Cape Breton session was found. The Plough and Stars' 1975 opening date comes from a search summary of an SF Legacy Business report that could not be opened (medium confidence). 'Fifth/5th String Music' as a Berkeley shop was not verified (the Side Door @ Fifth String Music is in Sacramento). [sf-song.json] Thread covered song/listening/singing/radio/shops/festivals only; instrumental sessions and dance are left to other threads. The SFFMC community folk calendar (updated 10/20/2026) and the Nov-Dec 2026 folknik (PDF text extracted) were the backbone for 2026 recurring evidence; many entries rely on that single listing (marked medium). Verified directly in 2026: BASH schedule, maritime.org chantey listings, KPFA/KALW show pages, Freight 990 data, the BOTMC 2026 contest, Kitka events, Starry Plough and Hotel Utah/Bazaar/Sweetwater open-mic listings (bayareaopenmics updated May-Aug 2026). Source disagreements: Freight capacity 450 vs 490; BOTMC revival 2003 vs 2004; Northwestern archive purchase 1973 vs 1974; Cabale opening 1962 vs 1963; BFUU open mic 1st vs 3rd Friday; chantey sing time 8pm-midnight aboard the Eureka (older sources) vs 6pm at the Maritime Museum (2026 calendar); KPFA Across the Great Divide host Kevin Vance (KPFA) vs Robbie Osman (older NCBS list). Not found or not verified: SFFMC and BASH membership numbers; HSB attendance after 2011; founding date of regular Bay Area Sacred Harp singings; KPFA show start years; Throckmorton Theatre / 142 Throckmorton folk programming; any Gert Chiarito link to KPFA's Midnight Special (sources credit Barry Olivier); whether Peter Kasin still leads the chantey sing; a living gospel-quartet circuit; Trio Kavkasia's Bay Area link (it formed in 1994 and does not appear Bay Area-based now); status of Subway Guitars and 5th String. Web search was heavily rate-limited; Nominatim returned 429 and thesession.org returned 403, so nearly all lat/lng are null (only the Freight has coordinates, from Wikipedia). Online-only events (SFFMC Zoom, virtual chantey sing, Jamulus singing) and the Palo Alto Sacred Harp singing (outside MSA) are listed but excluded from in-person totals.
